comparison: Perfect agreement on LPS uptake control experiments (C57, C58). Both recognize this as valid methodological control data showing NAD+ does not affect LPS internalization. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, peer reviewers do not challenge the finding.

Significant disagreement on interpretation. Both address survival and bacterial load claims (C22, C23, C30-C33, C38, C45). OpenEval finds the evidence well-supported for protection via inflammatory modulation. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'solid evidence' for protection but rate UNCERTAIN, stating the mechanism is 'unclear and needs further support' and that disease tolerance concept is inadequately discussed.

Strong agreement on cytokine and organ protection data (C24, C36-C37, C42-C44). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval describes data as well-supported by ELISA and histology. Peer reviewers call this 'solid evidence' for protective effects without challenge.

Disagreement on sufficiency of in vitro inflammasome data (C47, C49-C56, C60-C61). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on Western blots, time-course, and live microscopy showing pathway specificity. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting data is 'interesting' but 'unclear how the cell culture model reflects the animal model' and requesting additional experiments with primary cells from knockout animals.

Both address IFN-β pathway claims but with different scope. OpenEval R6 covers RNA-seq downregulation data (C62-C63, C67-C69, C74, C109) and rates SUPPORTED. Peer R4 includes these plus rescue experiments (C76-C78, C111, C113-C114) but rates UNCERTAIN, stating 'precise mechanisms remain unclear' and the link to bacterial infection/LPS model is 'not convincing.'

OpenEval R7 focuses on IFN-β rescue experiments (C71-C72, C76-C78, C111, C113-C114) showing mechanistic link and rates SUPPORTED based on complete reversal data. Peer R4 includes overlapping claims (C76-C78, C111, C113-C114) within broader IFN pathway evaluation but rates UNCERTAIN, requiring further elaboration of the mechanistic link.

Both address caspase-11-independent pathway (C81-C84, C115-C116). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on survival data in casp-11 KO mice showing dual mechanisms, though notes exact pathway needs characterization. Peer R5 includes these with IL-10 data and rates UNCERTAIN, requesting further experiments with primary cells from knockout animals and better integration of disease tolerance concept.

Both address IL-10 mechanism (C89-C90, C93-C96). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on flow cytometry, neutralization, and IL-10-/- mouse data. Peer R5 includes these claims in broader dual mechanism evaluation, acknowledges 'valuable contribution' but rates UNCERTAIN, requesting additional experiments with primary cells from knockout animals.

Major disagreement on auto/alloimmunity claims (C133, C135). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as interpretive conclusion based on combined data from current and previous work. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, explicitly challenging that 'no data that supports this statement is shown' in current work and requiring proper citation if referring to previous publications.

Disagreement on sepsis definition context (C1, C6, C7). OpenEval rates these background claims as SUPPORTED, describing them as appropriately cited literature context. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, stating 'the definition of sepsis is outdated' and that Sepsis-3 definition must be used instead of SIRS-based Sepsis-2 framework.

Minimal overlap on integrative conclusion (C100). OpenEval R10 rates dual mechanism conclusion as SUPPORTED by combined evidence. Peer R1 includes C100 in evaluation of bacterial clearance claims but rates UNCERTAIN due to unclear mechanism and inadequate discussion of disease tolerance.

OpenEval R5 addresses human macrophage translational relevance data (C60) and rates SUPPORTED for demonstrating cross-species conservation. No standalone peer review result addresses this claim, though C60 appears in peer R3's broader evaluation of in vitro data.
OpenEval R11 addresses preserved NF-κB expression (C132) as evidence of pathway specificity, rated SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim.

OpenEval R13 addresses speculative claims about caspase-8 and interferon regulatory factors (C127, C129, C131), appropriately rated UNCERTAIN as hypotheses for future work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval R14 addresses speculation about partial LDH reversal (C124), rated UNCERTAIN as untested hypothesis. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R15 addresses prior published work citations (C20-C21, C75, C87-C88, C117-C118), rated SUPPORTED as appropriate context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer R7 raises related concerns about citation practices.
OpenEval R17 addresses methodological descriptions for Figure 1 (C136-C142), rated SUPPORTED as accurate descriptions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these descriptive claims.

Peer R5 includes claim C5 and C27 (not in any OpenEval result) as part of evaluation of dual mechanism and disease tolerance concept. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, emphasizing need to incorporate disease tolerance framework and metabolic adaptation concepts that authors did not adequately address.
